subject: Made-to-measure alcove cabinetry
hook: The thin strip that makes alcove units look built in.
ig:
The thin strip that makes alcove units look built in is often the part nobody notices. That's the point.

It's called a scribed filler. Here's why it matters:

Alcove walls in older homes are rarely straight. They lean, bulge round old plaster or step where a pipe was boxed in.
If the cabinet itself were cut to follow that line, the doors would hang crooked.
So the cabinet stays square, and a separate filler panel takes up the difference.
It's marked against the wall, trimmed to that exact line and fixed in place, in the same finish as the doors.

The result: no shadow gap, no caulk trying to hide a crack, and doors that still open and close as they should.

It's one of those details you only notice when it's missing. Which detail would you look at first on a fitted unit? Tell us below, and find our alcove furniture via the link in bio.
fb:
Here's a detail most people never notice on a good fitted unit, and that's exactly why it's there.

It's a filler panel. Because alcove walls are rarely straight, we keep the cabinet itself perfectly square so the doors hang right, then fit a filler strip that's scribed to follow the wall's exact shape. It closes the gap all the way up without a line of filler or sealant doing the work.

If you've ever seen a fitted unit with a dark gap down one side, this is what was missing.
